attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about creating nested block statements in your code by placing one block statement inside of another block statement.

questions.hint: What does a nested block statement look like?
questions.title: [Select one] A nested block statement is…

answers.text: A block statement inside of another block statement
A block statement with a bird function
A block statement that is not indented

questions.correctResponse: An example of a nested block statement is when a conditional that uses one or more block statements is nested inside the curly brackets of a loop or event. Each nested block statement is indented and contains its own set of curly brackets to place code inside of.

questions.hint: What symbols always surround a conditional statement?
questions.title: [Select one] A conditional statement has its own set of curly brackets.
questions.correctResponse: A conditional contains its own set of curly brackets to place code inside of.

questions.hint: What condition needs to be true in order for the game to end in a win?
questions.title: [Select one] What will happen if the countdown ends and the score equals 3?

answers.text: The game over win screen will appear, and the smiles effect will start.
The game over lose screen will appear, and the splatter effect will start.
Nothing, the code only runs when the score is greater than 4.

questions.correctResponse: When the countdown ends, if the score is greater than 4, the game will end in a win. Else, the game will end in a loss.

questions.hint: What word(s) should be used to create a second condition in a conditional statement?
questions.title: [Select one] How should the second condition be typed in the code in line 117?
questions.correctResponse: To create multiple conditions, use the key words: else if.

subgroups.title: Nested Block Statements!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about creating nested block statements in your code by placing one block statement inside of another block statement.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about conditionals and nested block statements. Nested block statements are created when code inside of curly brackets is placed inside of another chunk of code in curly brackets, such as placing a conditional inside of a forever loop. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Curly Brackets All the Way Down
badges.description: Use nested block statements to place one block statement inside another in JavaScript.

badges.title: If at First You Don’t Succeed
badges.description: Use  “if” and “if / else” statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: ...or Else
badges.description: Use an “else if” statement in JavaScript.

badges.title: Until the End of Time
badges.description: Use a forever loop in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hey I’m Walking Here
badges.description: Use the overlapsWith function to see if two sprites are overlapping.

badges.title: Gaming the System
badges.description: Use the setGameOverEffect and gameOver functions to customize game over screens.

badges.title: The Final Countdown
badges.description: Use the info.onCountdownEnd function to run code when the countdown reaches zero.

badges.title: Playing the Odds
badges.description: Use the Math.percentChance function inside an if statement to add randomness to a project.

badges.title: A Flair for the Dramatic
badges.description: Add a custom sprite effect to a sprite.

badges.title: Let’s Try That Again
badges.description: Use the game.reset function to restart a project.
